text:
Molecular formula: C₉H₁₁NO₂  
Index of hydrogen deficiency: (2·9 + 2 + 1 – 11)/2 = 5  
→ 5 π-bonds/rings.  A benzene ring (4) plus one C=O (1) fits this.

IR data  
• 3420 & 3325 cm⁻¹  – two N–H stretches → a primary amine (–NH₂).  
• 1720 cm⁻¹ – ester/acid carbonyl; amide C=O would appear lower (≈1650–1680 cm⁻¹).  
So the molecule is an aryl ester that also contains an –NH₂ group.

¹H NMR (δ, ppm)  
1.20 t (3 H) – CH₃ of an ethyl group next to O (O–CH₂–CH₃).  
4.50 q (2 H) – O–CH₂– of that ethyl group.  
4.0 bs (2 H) – NH₂ protons (broad singlet).  
7.0 d (2 H) / 8.0 d (2 H) – two doublets (AA′BB′ pattern) of a p-disubstituted benzene ring.

Match with options  

A. 4-Aminophenyl propionate – has a propyl (CH₃CH₂–) next to carbonyl; its CH₂ (–CO–CH₂–) would resonate near 2.3 ppm, not at 4.5 ppm.  
B. Ethyl 4-aminobenzoate – contains an ethyl ester (O–CH₂–CH₃) giving the 4.5 q / 1.2 t, an ester C=O at 1720 cm⁻¹, an NH₂ group (double N–H bands), and a p-disubstituted ring (two 2H doublets). Fits all data.  
C. N-(4-ethoxyphenyl)formamide – secondary amide (only one N–H stretch) and amide C=O (~1660 cm⁻¹), not 1720 cm⁻¹.  
D. 3-Ethoxybenzamide – primary amide (two N–H stretches) but amide C=O would be ~1650 cm⁻¹ and aromatic pattern would not be two 2H doublets (meta substitution).

Only choice B satisfies every piece of evidence.

Answer: B
